title: Light Sources and How Light Travels
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Light Sources and How Light Travels Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe how light travels from a source and how it interacts with objects and materials to form shadows and images (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on light sources, how light travels in straight lines, how we see, and transparent, translucent and opaque materials. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: We see when light from a source reaches our eyes, directly or after reflecting.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines from a source.

  • A light source gives off its own light: the Sun, a torch, a fire, a glow-worm. The Moon and mirrors only reflect light.
  • We see an object when light from a source bounces off it and travels into our eyes.
  • Transparent materials let most light through, translucent materials let some through, and opaque materials block it.
Example

Is the Moon a light source?

it does not make light

it reflects sunlight

Answer: no

Example

Cards with holes in a line, then one is moved. Why does the light disappear?

light travels in straight lines

it cannot bend around the card

Answer: the light is blocked

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Moon, a mirror or a reflector is a light source.
  • Drawing arrows from the eye to the object (light goes into the eye).
  • Mixing up translucent (some light gets through) and transparent (almost all gets through).

faq.q: How do we know light travels in straight lines?
faq.a: Beams of sunlight and torch beams in smoke are straight, shadows form behind objects, and you can only see a light through holes in cards when the holes are lined up.

faq.q: Is the Moon a light source?
faq.a: No. The Moon reflects light from the Sun. Light sources, such as the Sun, a torch or a glow-worm, give off their own light.

faq.q: What is the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque?
faq.a: Transparent materials such as clear glass let almost all light through. Translucent materials such as baking paper let some light through. Opaque materials such as wood block light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a firefly, a mirror, a sheet of white paper or the Moon?

items.q: Why do lighthouses have bright lamps on tall towers?
c: Light travels in straight lines, so a high light can be seen far out at sea.

items.q: How do we see a book in a lit room?
c: The book gives off its own light.

items.q: Which travels faster: light or sound?

items.q: Why can't we see anything in a completely dark room?

items.q: Why do shadows have the same outline as the object?
c: The object gives off dark light.

items.e: The edges of the shadow line up with the edges of the object.

items.q: In a room with no light at all, could you see a cat?
c: No. With no light, no light can reflect from it into your eyes.
Yes, if it is shiny or white.
Yes, a little, because objects glow.
Yes, if you wait for your eyes to get used to it.
items.e: We see objects when light reflects off them into our eyes. Dark is the absence of light.

items.q: Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
c: Light travels much faster than sound.
items.e: They happen at the same time.

items.q: Light travels about 300 000 km every second. How far does it travel in 5 seconds?

c: Light shines out of your eyes onto it.

c: It makes a sound you can see.
It reflects light from your eyes.
